prompt: Our Q3 user access review just found that an IT admin who left in February still has an active ERP account with superuser privileges. Walk me through evaluating this.
assertions: Frames it as an ITGC deficiency to evaluate through what it undermines: superuser write access to financial data/configurations for ~7 months spanning interim periods

Applies the severity ladder with correct definitions (AS 2201 Appendix A / Reg S-X 1-02(a)(4)): deficiency → significant deficiency (merits oversight attention) → material weakness (reasonable possibility of material misstatement not prevented/detected)

Evaluates likelihood and magnitude properly: was the account USED (activity/log review), what could superuser access misstate (magnitude potentially unbounded), gross exposure before compensating controls
Tests compensating controls at precision before crediting them, and considers AGGREGATION with other access deficiencies on the same systems/assertions

Leans toward material-weakness territory if the account was usable with no monitoring — and covers the response: immediate revocation, activity forensics, root cause in the termination process, remediation with re-test window, audit-committee communication
